brief:
[c1] Further, HRMP plans to construct an overbuild with a construction cost of approximately $60 million as part of one of the casino’s garages, to serve as the platform for a Taste of Queens food hall that is being built by the New York Mets.
[c2] Because the Applicant repeatedly referred to the Taste of Queens as a core project element in its presentations to the community, however, the Board strongly believes that HRMP has an obligation to complete the food hall.
[c3] Those projects accordingly were not considered in the Board’s evaluation, but were raised during the Community Advisory Committee process, and the Board recommends to the Commission that the Applicant’s license require those projects to be completed.
[c4] As discussed in our Application (see EvalEconCaliber5.HardRock.RetailRecOther), HRMP will unlock further development potential within Metropolitan Park by delivering a parking podium on which Queens Baseball Company (i.e., the New York Mets) will then build the Taste of Queens.
[c5] The market will accommodate approximately 20 local food vendors, and we plan to partner with local groups to ensure that includes a mix of operators coming from both brick-and-mortar and street vendor origins.

checks.explanation: The original plan is documented in HRMP’s own response: “HRMP will… deliver[] a parking podium on which Queens Baseball Company (i.e., the New York Mets) will then build the Taste of Queens.” A later board report describes the same plan as “construct[ing] an overbuild… to serve as the platform for a Taste of Queens food hall that is being built by the New York Mets.” Together these establish HRMP’s role was to deliver the platform/podium for the food hall, while the Mets would build the hall itself.

The excerpts do not document an original HRMP pledge or proposal term that HRMP itself would complete the Taste of Queens food hall. Instead, HRMP’s documented plan says it would deliver “a parking podium on which Queens Baseball Company (i.e., the New York Mets) will then build the Taste of Queens,” and the board report likewise says the platform would serve a food hall “that is being built by the New York Mets.” The statement that “the Board strongly believes that HRMP has an obligation to complete the food hall” is the Board’s belief, not an original HRMP-stated commitment, and the recommendation that the license “require those projects to be completed” is also not an original HRMP proposal term.

c6.excerpt: As discussed in our Application (see EvalEconCaliber5.HardRock.RetailRecOther), HRMP will unlock further development potential within Metropolitan Park by delivering a parking podium on which Queens Baseball Company (i.e., the New York Mets) will then build the Taste of Queens. Detailed design for the interior of the Taste of Queens is still underway. We currently anticipate that the market (“food hall”) will be located on the elevated first floor, directly accessible and visible from the MTA gateway plaza as well as the open space. The market will accommodate approximately 20 local food vendors, and we plan to partner with local groups to ensure that includes a mix of operators coming from both brick-and-mortar and street vendor origins. We look forward to working with our community partners on further programmatic details in the years ahead before grand opening.

The main unresolved issue is whether the Commission later imposed a license condition requiring HRMP to complete the food hall despite that earlier division of roles.
